targets.outcome_reasoning: The abstract explicitly declares successful replication and extension of Experiments 1A and 2 to 4 as a set. This is an overall verdict, so codebook outcome rule 1 takes precedence. The discussion also reports successful replication of all original significant effects. Nevertheless, hypotheses 2 and 3 receive partial support and the report explicitly contrasts emotion/disgust specificity with the original, including in its conclusion. Without the abstract's overall verdict the agreeing and contrasting comparisons would support mixed. These are substantive contrasts, not merely reduced effect sizes. The authors do not state that this attempt is uninformative or that methodological invalidity is its main message.

reasoning: The report recruited a new American MTurk sample, completed data collection and reported results, combining the target experiments in one mixed-design experiment. The replication sample supplies the empirical test; published original statistics supply comparison benchmarks and effect-size/power calculations. Calculations from published statistics and pre-/post-exclusion analyses of the replication data are not re-analysis of original participant data. Only Young and Saxe (2011) is a target. Sweetman and Newman (2020) is an earlier replication discussed as background. Parkinson and Byrne and other cited studies provide motivation, extension context, or discussion comparisons rather than independently specified replication targets. Moral responsibility is presented as an extension of the Young and Saxe replication. Experiment 1B is described in the appendix but excluded from the abstract's stated target set; this study uses second-person materials. The target citation and DOI are printed in front matter under 'Citation of the target research article'; there is no separate Young and Saxe entry in the main reference list. All supplied report text and embedded supplementary sections through the final page were read. Coding is confined to supplied evidence.
